definitions.explanation: Refers to a quantity of two or more. Used both as a grammatical term (plural number) and in everyday language to mean 'multiple' or 'several.' The opposite of 単数 (singular).

examples.japanese: {複数|ふくすう}の{候補|こうほ}から{選|えら}ぶ。
{英語|えいご}では{名詞|めいし}に{単数|たんすう}と{複数|ふくすう}の{区別|くべつ}がある。
examples.english: In English, nouns have a distinction between singular and plural.

examples.japanese: {複数|ふくすう}の{目撃者|もくげきしゃ}が{同|おな}じ{証言|しょうげん}をした。
examples.english: Multiple witnesses gave the same testimony.

notes:
USAGE:
{複数|ふくすう} is commonly used as a pre-noun modifier: {複数|ふくすう}の + noun. In grammar, it refers to the plural form. In everyday use, it is a slightly formal way to say "multiple" or "several." Japanese nouns do not have grammatical plural forms, so this concept is mainly encountered when learning other languages.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {複数|ふくすう}の{人|ひと}: multiple people
- {複数|ふくすう}{形|けい}: plural form (grammar)
- {複数|ふくすう}{回|かい}: multiple times
- {複数|ふくすう}の{選択肢|せんたくし}: multiple options
- {単数|たんすう}・{複数|ふくすう}: singular and plural

SIMILAR WORDS:
{複数|ふくすう} is somewhat formal. In casual speech, {何人|なんにん}か (some people), いくつか (some, several), or {数|すう}〜 (several ~) are more natural. {多数|たすう} (majority, many) implies a larger quantity than {複数|ふくすう}.
